clue.text: Man with limitless libido turns out to be an MP

indicators.note: something that turns out a new way is reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: libido loses its limit, the final O, before joining the mix

explanation.surface: A sex-obsessed man is revealed to be a Member of Parliament, a tabloid scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limitless' trims only the final O from LIBIDO, leaving LIBID; MAN + LIBID rearranged by 'turns out' gives the surname. The Miliband brothers, Ed and David, were both Labour MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: Miliband is the surname of two prominent Labour Members of Parliament, so the name stands for an MP.

clue.text: Shot game

definitions.meaning: a photograph, a quick shot taken with a camera
a children's card game where matching cards are slapped down

explanation.definitionFit: A snap is both a quick photograph and a simple card game for children.

clue.text: Party leader finding Cockney woman an unattractive person

parts.note: Menzies 'Ming' Campbell led the Liberal Democrats when this puzzle appeared
a Cockney drops the H of 'her', saying 'er

explanation.surface: A political leader is said to find a London woman unappealing to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: Ming Campbell was leader of the UK Liberal Democrat party; Cockney is the dialect of working-class east London, which drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Minger is British slang for someone considered very unattractive.

clue.text: Never leave

definitions.meaning: the exclamation of disbelief '...!' means 'Never!' or 'You don't say!'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works as a disbelieving exclamation like 'No way!' and as a verb meaning escape or depart.

clue.text: A slender model for an artist

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thin figure serves as a model posing for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' is the anagram signal on A SLENDER. Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian English painter of animals who also sculpted the lions in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin Landseer was a celebrated Victorian painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Deliver princess's eulogy

parts.note: Princess Diana was widely called Di, so the possessive gives DI'S
a eulogy is a spoken tribute of praise, often at a funeral

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to give a speech in praise of a princess.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests delivering a speech, Earl Spencer's eulogy for Diana, but 'Deliver' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute is to hand out or deliver goods to the people meant to receive them.

clue.text: Bells originally found on Indian ladies' fingers

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word bells

parts.note: Hindi is the main language of northern India

explanation.surface: Bells are found on the fingers of Indian women, as jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladies' fingers' looks like part of the jewellery picture, but it is another name for okra, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhindi is the Indian name for okra, which is also called ladies' fingers.

clue.text: VIP is being awkward about nothing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go round the zero
awkward means clumsy or out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: An important person is being difficult over a trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' makes BIGNISE; 'about' wraps that round the zero. 'nothing' reads as 'a trifle' in the surface, but it gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A big noise is an informal name for an important, influential person.

clue.text: Clapham is, historically, home to a sect

indicators.note: the words are a home that houses the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Clapham, in south London, was once where a religious group lived.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across claphAM IS Historically. Clapham was in fact home to the Clapham Sect of evangelical reformers, which makes the false trail convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a traditionalist Christian community, a religious sect.

clue.text: Detective meeting politician and solicitor

parts.note: PI stands for private investigator, a detective
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A detective meets a politician and a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer, a British legal profession, but here it is one who solicits for prostitutes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimp solicits clients on behalf of prostitutes, so he is literally a solicitor.

clue.text: Show off fine stomach

parts.note: grand means fine or splendid
to stomach something is to stand or tolerate it

explanation.surface: An instruction to display a good, flat belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stomach' reads as a noun but is the verb meaning put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To grandstand is to behave showily to win attention from onlookers.

clue.text: Father without time for glib talk

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for father goes round

parts.note: pater is Latin for father, used in old-fashioned British slang

explanation.surface: A father with no time to spare for smooth talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking, so PATER surrounds T.
explanation.definitionFit: Patter is the rapid, slick talk of a salesman or entertainer.

clue.text: Some turned out to be fantastic

indicators.note: out means not in proper order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A few things turned out to be wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like one phrase, but 'turned' is fodder and 'out' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous and fantastic are both informal words for excellent.

clue.text: A spirit's the heart of stiff drink

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or spirit of Persian legend

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters, here of stiff

explanation.surface: A spirit lies at the heart of a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests alcohol, but it is the peri of Persian myth; the heart of sTIFf is TIF.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is a drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Was devoted to dizzy redhead

indicators.note: dizzy means spinning and confused, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was infatuated with a scatterbrained ginger-haired woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To have adhered to something is to have stuck to it faithfully, to have been devoted.

clue.text: Confronts Brownite about the old

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the politician's name goes round the old word

parts.note: Ed Balls was a close ally of Gordon Brown, a Brownite, written here as E. Balls
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: Someone stands up to a supporter of Gordon Brown about the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was UK Chancellor, then Prime Minister. His ally Ed Balls appears as initial plus surname, and 'about' puts that round the old word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare them down, confronting them face to face.

clue.text: Thailand's currency causing concern

parts.note: T is the international vehicle registration code for Thailand
the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: The Thai currency is causing worry.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the baht, but 'Thailand's' gives only T and the currency is Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble and concern both mean worry or a cause of anxiety.

clue.text: A red kind of rabbit?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: lop or cut off the E from EARED, which leaves ARED, the words a red

explanation.surface: A question about what sort of rabbit has red fur.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as an order to lop E from EARED, produces 'A red'. A lop-eared rabbit has drooping ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Lop-eared rabbits, with long drooping ears, are a popular domestic breed type.

clue.text: Terribly infectious typhoid at first found in most bats and birds

indicators.note: found in means placed within, so the initials go inside
bats is slang for crazy, so the letters of most are rearranged
at first takes the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Typhoid caught from bats and birds is horribly contagious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like animals, but it signals the anagram that gives TOMS. 'found in' puts the three initials inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomtits are small birds, a familiar name for the blue tit and similar species.

clue.text: Organised last of the purges, having no conscience

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged
last of takes the final letter of the word the

parts.note: no is nought, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Organised purges carried out by people lacking any moral sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests ruthless purges without conscience; in Freudian theory that conscience is the superego, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freud's model the superego is the part of the mind acting as moral conscience.

clue.text: Local individual's just rough

parts.note: 'un is a dialect form of one, an individual, as in 'a good 'un'
even means fair or just

explanation.surface: A local person's simply crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' reads as merely but means fair, giving EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven means not smooth or level, so rough.

clue.text: Mountaineer perhaps losing power to move

indicators.note: to move means the remaining letters shift into a new order
losing means one letter is dropped from the word perhaps

explanation.surface: A climber may lose the strength to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: PERHAPS loses one P to leave ERHAPS, which 'to move' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famed as expert climbers and guides, so a Sherpa is a mountaineer.

clue.text: He discussed philosophy in prestigious Art Review

indicators.note: in means the answer lies within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A philosopher was debated in a respected arts magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans prestigiouS ART REview.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre was a French existentialist who wrote and argued about philosophy.

clue.text: Principal reads them a novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school head reads a novel to the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book being read, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal is the head of a school, the same role as a headmaster.

clue.text: Heartless Kazakhstani hooker?

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is taken away

parts.note: Borat is the fictional Kazakh reporter played by Sacha Baron Cohen

explanation.surface: A cruel Kazakh prostitute, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooker' suggests a prostitute, but a hooker is a small fishing boat; Borat minus its middle R gives BOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooker is a one-masted fishing vessel, so it is an example of a boat, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Clinton shortly will start to barnstorm for wife

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another, replacing the abbreviation for wife
start to takes the opening letter of barnstorm

explanation.surface: Clinton will soon start to campaign on behalf of his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: In WILL, B replaces W. Barnstorming is touring to campaign, apt for Bill backing Hillary.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill is the short form of William, the first name of President Clinton.

clue.text: Vote at last in capacity of Liberal peer

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of the word vote

parts.note: qua is Latin for in the capacity of

explanation.surface: A Liberal member of the House of Lords finally votes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' suggests a lord, but it means someone of equal standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is one's equal in age, rank or ability.

clue.text: He sings about heroin, bringing out top selling album

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the singer goes round the drug

parts.note: a triller is one who trills, singing with warbles
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A singer on drugs releases a bestselling record.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Jackson's Thriller is the best-selling album of all time, fitting a surface about a drug-troubled singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thriller by Michael Jackson is widely cited as the best-selling album ever.
